overviewHtml:
This graded quiz assesses your understanding of Merleau-Ponty's late philosophy. You'll be asked about his self-critique, flesh, reversibility, and the chiasm, and the reframing of subject, world, and nature.

Note: Aim for a score of 80 percent or higher. If you score lower, use the feedback to review the topics you missed, then retake the quiz.

forms.stemHtml: In what sense does Merleau-Ponty come to see Phenomenology of Perception as a philosophy of consciousness?

options.html: It claims that only minds exist
options.text: It claims that only minds exist
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the consciousness–object starting point and the tacit cogito.

options.html: It starts from a subject to whom things appear
options.text: It starts from a subject to whom things appear
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Even an embodied subject, taken as the starting point, makes the world a world for consciousness.

options.html: It ignores the body in favor of thought
options.text: It ignores the body in favor of thought
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the consciousness–object starting point and the tacit cogito.

options.html: It relies on introspective reports from experiments
options.text: It relies on introspective reports from experiments
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the consciousness–object starting point and the tacit cogito.

forms.stemHtml: What is Merleau-Ponty's objection to a philosophy of reflection?

options.html: It relies too heavily on the senses
options.text: It relies too heavily on the senses
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on reflection, intuition, dialectic, and hyper-reflection.

options.html: It forgets its origin in unreflected experience
options.text: It forgets its origin in unreflected experience
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Reflection begins in a perceived world and then treats that world as its own product.

options.html: It refuses to think about consciousness
options.text: It refuses to think about consciousness
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on reflection, intuition, dialectic, and hyper-reflection.

options.html: It depends on the study of animals
options.text: It depends on the study of animals
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on reflection, intuition, dialectic, and hyper-reflection.

forms.stemHtml: What is the term for the silent, pre-reflective presence of the self to itself that the earlier Merleau-Ponty placed beneath every explicit act of reflection, and later judged impossible? Enter two words.

options.html: tacit cogito
options.text: tacit cogito
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Removing it removed the last foundation of the philosophy of consciousness.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the consciousness–object starting point and the tacit cogito.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following does Merleau-Ponty deny that flesh is?

options.html: A general way of being shared by body and world
options.text: A general way of being shared by body and world
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on flesh as element and the visibility of the seer.

options.html: An element in the old sense
options.text: An element in the old sense
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on flesh as element and the visibility of the seer.

options.html: Matter, mind, or substance
options.text: Matter, mind, or substance
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Flesh is none of the three traditional candidates.

options.html: The visibility and tangibility of things
options.text: The visibility and tangibility of things
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on flesh as element and the visibility of the seer.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are examples Merleau-Ponty's late ontology uses for reversibility? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: One hand touching the other
options.text: One hand touching the other
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is the central example.

options.html: A handshake with another person
options.text: A handshake with another person
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! I touch and am touched by another's hand.

options.html: The seer who is also visible
options.text: The seer who is also visible
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Reversibility extends to vision.

options.html: A thermometer registering heat
options.text: A thermometer registering heat
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on reversibility, the chiasm, and Husserl's touching hands.

options.html: A computer processing an image
options.text: A computer processing an image
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on reversibility, the chiasm, and Husserl's touching hands.

forms.stemHtml: What is Merleau-Ponty's term for the relation by which touching and touched, or seeing and seen, can exchange roles, always imminent but never fully realized? Enter one word.

options.html: reversibility
options.text: reversibility
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The roles reverse but never coincide.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on reversibility, the chiasm, and Husserl's touching hands.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are widely recognized strengths of the flesh ontology? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: It overcomes dualism at the level of starting point
options.text: It overcomes dualism at the level of starting point

options.html: It grounds continuity between mind and life
options.text: It grounds continuity between mind and life
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Consciousness needn't be an anomaly in nature.

options.html: It proves that nature is conscious
options.text: It proves that nature is conscious

options.html: It settles every objection its critics raised
options.text: It settles every objection its critics raised

forms.stemHtml: Why does starting from the consciousness–object distinction leave the earlier book's problems unsolvable?

options.html: The problems were about language, which the book ignored

forms.stemHtml: Why does Merleau-Ponty find Sartre's opposition of being and nothingness inadequate?

options.html: Because it denies that consciousness exists
options.text: Because it denies that consciousness exists

options.text: Because it relies on scientific measurement

options.html: Because the opposition is itself a dualism
options.text: Because the opposition is itself a dualism
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! It sees the world from above, laid out for a thought that isn't part of it.

options.html: Because it ignores the problem of other minds
options.text: Because it ignores the problem of other minds
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on reflection, intuition, dialectic, and hyper-reflection.

forms.stemHtml: What is Merleau-Ponty's term, translating être sauvage, for being as it is encountered before it is divided into subject and object? Enter two words.

options.html: wild being

forms.stemHtml: Why does Merleau-Ponty hold that the seer's visibility is a condition of seeing?

options.text: Because the seer sees from within the visible it belongs to

options.html: Because vision requires light reflected from our eyes
options.text: Because vision requires light reflected from our eyes

options.html: Because we can only see what resembles us
options.text: Because we can only see what resembles us

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are true of the hinge (charnière) in Merleau-Ponty's working notes? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: It's where perceiver and perceived turn into each other
options.text: It's where perceiver and perceived turn into each other
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The two sides are articulated at the hinge.

options.html: It joins the two sides without merging them
options.text: It joins the two sides without merging them
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Like two leaves of a door on one pin.

options.html: It's a physical joint in the body
options.text: It's a physical joint in the body
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on divergence and the hinge.

options.html: It eliminates the gap between perceiver and perceived
options.text: It eliminates the gap between perceiver and perceived
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on divergence and the hinge.

forms.stemHtml: What English term translates Merleau-Ponty's écart, the spacing that keeps perceiver and perceived distinct within their reversibility? Enter one word.

options.html: divergence
options.text: divergence
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! It's structural, not a failure.

options.html: gap
options.text: gap
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! It's structural, not a failure.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on divergence and the hinge.

options.html: Because others are only known by inference

options.html: Because the ethical relation is asymmetrical
options.text: Because the ethical relation is asymmetrical

options.html: Because reversibility is complete

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following describe the flesh ontology's uptake? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Thompson argues for continuity between life and mind

forms.stemHtml: What are the private, dated notes that Merleau-Ponty wrote while drafting The Visible and the Invisible, published with it after his death, usually called? Enter two words.
